Primitive FFI Call

Source: R/primitives.R
prim_custom_call.Rd

Invokes an XLA FFI handler registered with pjrt::pjrt_register_custom_call(). XLA documents custom calls, and the FFI API a handler is written against, in its custom call guide.

This is the escape hatch for operations StableHLO cannot express, or cannot express efficiently. Unlike every other primitive, its output types cannot be derived from its inputs – the handler decides them – so they are declared up front.

Custom calls exist only on the "pjrt" backend, which is the one that compiles StableHLO and runs the handler. There is no quickr rule and there cannot be one, so a function containing a custom call fails to compile under local_backend("quickr").

Within pjrt the call is platform-agnostic: it names a target, and XLA invokes whichever handler was registered for the platform the program is compiled for. Registering a cuda handler alongside the cpu one is therefore all it takes to run the same call on a GPU.

Use nv_custom_call() unless you need the exact primitive signature.

Usage

prim_custom_call(
  operands,
  target_name,
  output_types = NULL,
  attrs = list(),
  has_side_effect = is.null(output_types),
  operand_layouts = NULL,
  result_layouts = NULL,
  aliases = NULL,
  device = NULL
)

Arguments

operands

(list of arrayish)
The values passed to the handler, in the order it binds them.

target_name

(character(1))
The name the handler was registered under.

output_types

(AbstractArray | list of them | NULL)
Data type and shape of each result. The handler, not the inputs, decides these, so anvl cannot infer them. NULL declares a call that only runs for its side effect; operands are then returned unchanged, so at least one is required.

attrs

(list)
Named attributes the handler reads via .Attr<T>("name") or .Attrs<Dictionary>(). A string is converted for you, and so is a number or a logical, at a data type fixed by its R type, whatever default_dtypes() says: a double is f64, an integer i64 and a logical bool, so the handler reads them as double, int64_t and bool. A vector of several becomes an array attribute of that data type. Pass a stablehlo attribute object such as stablehlo::ScalarAttr() for another data type.

has_side_effect

(logical(1))
Whether XLA must keep the call even when its results are unused. Defaults to TRUE exactly when output_types is NULL. Under gradient(), a side-effect call in the body of an nv_scan() may still be dropped.

operand_layouts, result_layouts

(list | NULL)
The memory layout of each operand and result: its axes in minor-to-major order, the axis whose index varies fastest in memory first. NULL (the default) is R's own column-major order, seq_len(n) for an n-axis array, which is how a LAPACK routine wants a matrix. A handler written for row-major (C order) buffers wants rev(seq_len(n)) instead. Keep the default for a call that may see an array with an axis of size zero: XLA's CPU compiler crashes compiling any other layout for one.

A handler whose platforms disagree – a LAPACK CPU kernel wanting column-major next to a row-major CUDA one – can instead pass a list of such lists named by platform, e.g. list(cpu = list(1:2), cuda = list(2:1)). The entry is picked when the program is lowered, which is the first point at which the target platform is known.

aliases

(integer() | NULL)
One entry per result, giving the index of the operand whose buffer that result is written into, or NA for no aliasing. XLA then hands the handler the same pointer for both, so an in-place kernel avoids a copy.

device

(NULL | character(1) | device)
Where to run. Only needed when there are no operands to take it from.

Value

list of arrayish
One element per result, or the operands unchanged for a side-effect only call.
